summary.headline: Aurobindo Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record ₹10,263 crore (+24% YoY) with operating EBITDA ₹2,156 crore (21% margin); FY27 guidance reiterated.
summary.overview: Revenue of ₹10,263 crore grew 24% YoY, the highest ever quarter, with Formulations at ₹9,102 crore (89%) and API at ₹1,162 crore (11%). Operating EBITDA rose 28% YoY to ₹2,156 crore at a 21% margin despite higher input and freight costs, and gross margin improved to 61.2% from 59.7%. Lannett was consolidated for the first time this quarter, with the US business at USD 477 million (+25% YoY) and Europe at €288 million (+18% constant currency). Management reiterated FY27 guidance of double-digit revenue growth, EBITDA margin above 21% and absolute EBITDA above ₹8,000 crore, and said FY28 should be better than FY27.

financial_highlights.value: USD 189 million; quarterly cash flow USD 146 million

segments.name: US
segments.commentary: Revenue USD 477 million (₹4,555 crore), +25% YoY. Launched 10 products, filed 7 ANDAs and received 12 final approvals in the quarter. gAdvair launched mid-quarter, so benefit was limited in Q2.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue €288 million, +18% constant currency. Management cited supply from Vizag Unit 15 and China, and air-freighted urgent products. Management expects growth to be sustained.

segments.name: Growth markets
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹1,026 crore (USD 107 million), +16% YoY. ARV formulations were USD 38 million on stable volume.

segments.name: Lannett (US, acquired)
segments.commentary: Consolidated this quarter, contributing around ₹200 crore per the CFO. Management said its EBITDA is in line with or better than group EBITDA; Lannett's facility remains underutilised and CDMO is only 10-15% of its capacity.

segments.name: China OSD facility
segments.commentary: Around 15 products supplied; breakeven expected this quarter. First-half opex loss about USD 3-4 million, with about USD 1 million in the last quarter.

segments.name: Pen-G / API
segments.commentary: API revenue ₹1,162 crore (+21%). Pen-G producing about 10,000 tonnes against 15,000 tonnes capability; Indian demand about 9,000 tonnes. Pen-G EBITDA positive but small and expected to rise significantly, excluding PLI benefit. 6-APA prices recently increased.

segments.name: Eugia
segments.commentary: Management said it is growing double digits every quarter and is back at full production capacity. Revenue mix is roughly US 55%, rest of world 45%, moving toward 50:50 in FY28-FY29.

guidance_outlook: FY27: double-digit revenue growth, EBITDA margin north of 21%, absolute EBITDA above ₹8,000 crore, with potential upside from high-value strategic businesses.
EBITDA margin expected to reach upwards of 22% in the coming years (FY28), per management; the analyst's 28% reference was corrected to 22%.
FY28 expected to be better than FY27, driven by full-year Lannett, China ramp-up and biosimilars.
China facility breakeven expected in Q2 FY27.
Pen-G capacity could reach about 12,000 tonnes by next year; aggressive ramp expected in about six months as regulatory approvals come through.
capex_capacity: Total capex in Q2 was USD 89 million: USD 47 million for development capabilities and USD 42 million for strategic priorities. Management said maintenance and development spend runs at about USD 50 million per quarter, with around USD 200 million annual run rate.
H1 capex of about ₹1,600 crore includes strategic spend on biologics CDMO and intangible assets for partner products.
Raleigh (US) received VAI classification. Capacity utilisation is nominal because MDI manufacturing has not started; management expects improvement in 6-9 months.
Pen-G: capability of 15,000 tonnes; current output about 10,000 tonnes.
Lannett is underutilised; management is pursuing CDMO and new product filings to fill capacity.
demand_pricing: Gross margin rose to 61.2% from 59.7%, supported by product mix, procurement and operating leverage.
Higher raw material costs from the Gulf situation have not yet fully flowed into consumption and will do so in coming quarters.
Freight costs rose; the CFO expects quarterly operating expenses (ex-R&D and COGS) around ₹2,450 crore going forward, up from about ₹2,400 crore in Q2 and ₹2,150 crore in Q1.
Europe: management expects double-digit growth to continue, citing launches, late-to-launch products and CuraTeQ and Eugia products.
Biosimilars: management said it will be selective and partner-led, not chase Sandoz- or Fresenius-scale portfolios.
Pomalidomide: shared exclusivity with multiple players; management described it as a decent contributor, not a major opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: Margin trajectory and time frame for the longer-term target?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO corrected the target to 22% (not 28%). Levers: Lannett integration and yields, China ramp-up, biosimilars and biologics.

qa_highlights.question: Is the China facility near breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakeven expected this quarter. Around 15 products are supplied from China, and first-half opex loss is about USD 3-4 million.

qa_highlights.question: Lannett's contribution and cost rationalisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Lannett's EBITDA is in line with or better than group EBITDA. SG&A rationalisation is under way in phases and is reflected in results. Management did not disclose a revenue figure, though the CFO cited about ₹200 crore of Lannett contribution in the opex discussion.

qa_highlights.question: Respiratory inflection and Raleigh capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: gAdvair is launched; the in-house MDI is expected within months. Management expects a scaled-up respiratory business around mid-2029 across 3-4 products. Raleigh utilisation is nominal and should improve in 6-9 months.

qa_highlights.question: Pen-G pricing, anti-dumping and utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: 6-APA prices rose 10-15 days ago, with India impact in 15-20 days after existing stock clears. Anti-dumping duty filed and notified. Pen-G EBITDA is positive but small, with output around 10,000 tonnes against 15,000 tonnes capability.

qa_highlights.question: Europe sustainability at about €285 million quarterly base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no saturation, with growth ahead of the industry, launches and CuraTeQ/Eugia products to come, and climbing positions in some countries.

risks_watch: Raw material cost pressure from the Gulf situation and higher freight, which has not yet fully hit consumption.
Lannett integration and utilisation; the facility is underutilised and CDMO is only 10-15% of its capacity.
Early-stage launches (ADQUEY, gAdvair, MDI) with limited Q2 contribution and no market-share disclosure yet.
Pen-G margin depends on government policy, anti-dumping outcome and the PLI benefit.
Europe growth on a high base of about €285-288 million quarterly; management's sustainability claim is unquantified.
Biologics CDMO depends on a single anchor customer (MSD).
summary.management_tone: Confident on the headline numbers and FY27 guidance, but evasive on specifics. Management declined to disclose Lannett revenue, ADQUEY market share and pricing, and Europe and US product detail. It was also cautious on timelines, saying the respiratory inflection will take 12-18 months or more.
key_quotes: We reiterate our FY guidance with the double-digit revenue growth, EBITDA margins north of 21% and absolute EBITDA in excess of 8,000 crore.

adds.what: Pen-G capacity expansion to about 12,000 tonnes (from 15,000 t capability per brief; ramp expected after regulatory approvals)
Raleigh (US) MDI manufacturing, VAI-classified facility not yet started
China OSD facility ramp-up, breakeven expected this quarter (already operating)

growth.why: FY27 guidance reiterated: double-digit revenue growth, EBITDA margin above 21% and absolute EBITDA above ₹8,000 crore, with FY28 expected better, backed by Lannett full-year consolidation, China ramp, Pen-G ramp to ~12,000 t after approvals and Europe launches, though no new numbers were given and capacity timing is partly uncertain.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin rose to 61.2% from 59.7%, and management targets EBITDA margin of upwards of 22% in the coming years, with Lannett integration, China breakeven and biosimilars as levers, though opex and raw material pressure are rising.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Pen-G capability is 15,000 t with output around 10,000 t and a stated move to ~12,000 t after approvals in about six months, and Raleigh MDI is expected to start within 6-9 months, though timing depends on regulatory approvals.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides double-digit revenue growth for FY27, Europe growth is said to continue (Q2 +18% CC on €288 million), and Pen-G output can rise from ~10,000 t toward 15,000 t capability as approvals come through.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex runs about USD 50 million per quarter (USD 89 million in Q2) with an annual run rate near USD 200 million, but no new plant was announced and Pen-G (~10,000 t vs 15,000 t capability) and Lannett (underutilised) already offer spare capacity.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was reiterated with 'potential upside' from high-value strategic businesses, and FY27 EBITDA is above ₹8,000 crore against H1 EBITDA of about ₹4,000 crore-plus (Q2 alone was ₹2,156 crore), but no new numbers were given.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flagged Gulf-driven raw material costs that have not yet hit consumption and quarterly opex rising to about ₹2,450 crore from ₹2,400 crore in Q2, which could squeeze the 21% margin floor even though FY27 guidance was held.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Ten US products launched in Q2 with 7 ANDAs filed and 12 final approvals, and gAdvair launched mid-quarter with a full-quarter benefit still to come, plus the MDI launch expected within months.

rows.label: China OSD facility breakeven
rows.why: Around 15 products supplied from China, with first-half opex loss of about USD 3-4 million and breakeven guided for this quarter, then full-year China ramp in FY28.

rows.label: Lannett SG&A rationalisation and integration
rows.why: Lannett contributes around ₹200 crore per the CFO with EBITDA in line with or better than group, and SG&A cuts are under way in phases with CDMO only 10-15% of capacity, so utilisation and yields are the lever.

rows.label: Pen-G ramp and 6-APA price increase
rows.why: 6-APA prices rose 10-15 days before the call with India impact in 15-20 days, and Pen-G EBITDA is positive but small and expected to rise significantly, excluding PLI, subject to anti-dumping notification and approvals.

tone.note: Management was confident on the record Q2 and held FY27 guidance, and it corrected the FY28 margin target to 22% from 28%, but it was evasive on Lannett revenue, ADQUEY share and pricing; analysts pushed on margin trajectory, Lannett contribution and Europe sustainability.
